0.0.n: A hesitation sound used while preparing to speak.

0.2.n: Softens the introduction rather than adding factual information.

0.3.n: Makes the announcement sound less direct; it does not indicate a small quantity here.

0.4.n: A casual, modest way to refer to yourself, commonly used by men.

0.5.n: Joins the speaker and Jinto as the two people taking the role.

0.6.n: This is the first part of the name 仁人, split across subtitle tokens.

0.7.n: Completes 仁人 and adds 君, a familiar title often used for boys or male peers.

0.8.n: Marks 僕と仁人君 as the people becoming the prank organizers.

0.9.n: Refers to the people secretly arranging the prank, rather than its targets.

0.10.n: With なる, marks the role someone takes on.

0.11.n: The linking form of polite なります connects taking this role to the explanation that follows.

1.0.n: A polite acknowledgment of what was just said.

2.0.n: A softening filler before explaining what they will do.

2.2.n: Places the planned action at the current stage of proceedings.

2.4.n: This is the first part of the name 柔太朗, not a separate descriptive word.

2.5.n: Completes the name 柔太朗, which was split across subtitle tokens.

2.7.n: This is the first part of the name 舜太.

2.8.n: Completes the name 舜太; it is not an independent word here.

2.10.n: This is the first part of the name 太智.

2.11.n: Completes the name 太智, which was split across subtitle tokens.

2.12.n: Marks the three named people as the recipients of the upcoming instruction.

2.13.n: In にですね, です adds a polite pause rather than meaning is.

2.14.n: Seeks the listener's attention while the speaker continues explaining.

3.0.n: Softens the mention of filling out the questionnaire.

3.1.n: A borrowed word for a survey or its question sheet.

3.2.n: Marks the questionnaire as what someone will fill out.

3.3.n: The plain form of 書く refers here to writing answers on a questionnaire.

3.4.n: Gives filling out the questionnaire as the reason for moving to the room.

3.5.n: Refers to the program that the questionnaire is supposedly for.

3.6.n: Links 番組 to the earlier アンケート; the speaker adds this detail after mentioning the questionnaire.

4.1.n: Softens the request to write in the other room.

4.2.n: A casual expression indicating the room on this side or in this direction.

4.3.n: Connects こっち to 部屋, specifying which room.

4.4.n: Names the place where they are asked to complete the questionnaire.

4.5.n: Marks the location where the writing will happen.

4.6.n: The て-form of 書く is used by itself as a casual request.

4.8.n: Casual っていう introduces the quoted wording used to call them in.

4.9.n: In っていうふうに, describes the manner of calling them in.

4.10.n: Turns ふう into a description of how they will call the others in.

4.11.n: Polite form of 呼び出す, used here for getting people to come to a particular place.

5.0.n: A brief polite acknowledgment that the listener is following.

6.0.n: Refers back to the room where the prank targets will be brought.

6.2.n: A conversational filler while introducing examples.

6.4.n: The prefix お gives the everyday noun 水 a polite touch.

6.5.n: The connecting stem of だ before たり; together they introduce an example.

6.6.n: In だったり, presents water as one example rather than an exhaustive choice.

6.7.n: Reinforces that the speaker is giving an open-ended list.

7.0.n: The prefix お is commonly included in this everyday word for a packed meal.

7.1.n: The connecting stem of だ combines with たり to introduce another example.

7.2.n: Continues the example-listing pattern started with water.

7.3.n: Keeps the list open rather than limiting it to these items.

7.5.n: A sound-symbolic word for a sharp tingling sensation, describing the prank pen.

7.6.n: Together with ビリビリ, names a prank pen that gives an electric shock.

7.7.n: Closes the examples before the speaker sums them up as various prank setups.

7.8.n: A conversational form of いろいろな, used directly before a noun.

7.9.n: Refers to the tricks or mechanisms prepared to surprise the targets.

7.10.n: Marks the prank setups as the things already put in place.

7.11.n: The て-form of 施す plus あります shows that someone deliberately prepared them and they remain ready.

7.12.n: Gives the prepared traps as a reason for what the speaker will explain next.

0.lit: Um, well, just, I and Jinto take on the prank-organizer role, and…
0.tip: に plus なる expresses taking on a role; なりまして politely links this announcement to what follows.

1.tip: はい can simply acknowledge another person's explanation.

2.lit: Just, now, to Jyutaro, Shunta, and Daichi, you see…
2.tip: に marks the people who will receive the instruction in the following lines.

3.lit: Just, because they will fill out a questionnaire—for the show…
3.tip: 番組の is an afterthought describing the earlier questionnaire, a natural feature of spontaneous speech.

4.lit: We'll call them in by saying, Just fill it out in this room.
4.tip: 書いて is a casual request, while って introduces the words they plan to say.

5.tip: Here はい signals that the listener is following along.

6.lit: There, well, things like water, and such…
6.tip: Noun plus だったりとか introduces examples without claiming to list everything.

7.lit: Things like boxed lunches, shock pens, and various prank setups have been put in place, so…
7.tip: てあります emphasizes that something was deliberately prepared and remains in that state.
